name: setlist-a11y-fallback
note: SUPERSEDES setlist-remove-arm.json. Round 18 (operator UAT 2026-09-02) replaced the set row's two-tap arm-to-delete x with a SWIPE (either direction, >=25% of row width) and its grip-drag with PRESS-AND-HOLD on the row - see setlist-gestures.json for the gesture proofs. Both new gestures are pointer-only, so WCAG 2.5.1 (Pointer Gestures) requires a non-gesture equivalent: the up/down/remove buttons stay in the DOM on every set row, visually quiet at rest (.li-a11yctrl, the skip-link reveal-on-focus pattern) and revealed at full size on keyboard focus. THIS scenario is the proof that the fallback is real - it is the reason the old arm scenario could be retired rather than simply deleted. The remove fallback keeps the two-tap arm grammar (first activation arms, second removes), so a stray Enter never destroys a row.

steps.label: the a11y controls EXIST on every set row and are quiet at rest (1x1 clipped) - the sighted-pointer view stays clean now that the gestures own the row
REMOVE fallback is keyboard-reachable: focusable, tabbable, revealed to a full 44x44 target on focus, and carries a name that says WHICH song it removes
the remove fallback KEEPS the two-tap arm grammar - one activation arms, it does NOT destroy a row (a stray Enter must never delete)
the SECOND activation removes the row - the keyboard path reaches the same removeFromSet + undo the swipe uses
REORDER fallback works by keyboard: row 2's up-arrow focuses, reveals, and actually MOVES the row (press-and-hold is pointer-only, so this is the equivalent path)
the FIRST row's up-arrow is correctly disabled (nothing above it) - a disabled control is honest, not a broken fallback
